stories.notes: Empty AC on a complex multi-market (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature with real-time rendering, auth/token security, and draft/unpublished state edge cases. openspec needed first to elaborate requirements and draft AC; speckit then hardens with testability, security, and edge-case coverage. No existing spec or hand-curation detected.

agentContributions.notes: Story requests a new capability (Live Preview) not present in the codebase. The central attachment point is useContent, which 236 components rely on to fetch Contentstack content. Integrating Live Preview at that layer means all downstream components (ContentstackLink, ContentstackImage, ContentstackTable, ContentstackContentCards, etc.) inherit preview behavior without individual changes. Acceptance criteria were empty; VCs derived from the description alone.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with a useful architectural note about useContent being the central hub for 236+ components. I built the entire AC set from the story title, description, file list, and that architectural insight. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 separate the general real-time update requirement from component-type-specific coverage to make testability granular. (2) AC-3/AC-9/AC-14 form a three-layer safety net ensuring production never sees preview data, connections, or bundle weight. (3) AC-4/AC-5/AC-13 cover error/resilience scenarios — connection loss, recovery, and malformed data. (4) AC-6 addresses the initial-load race condition (published content first, then preview overlay). (5) AC-7 is the no-regression gate for the 236+ existing consumers of useContent. (6) AC-8 covers nested references since Contentstack entries commonly reference other entries. (7) AC-10 ensures cross-codebase parity since the story explicitly scopes GO, UP, MX. (8) AC-11 addresses concurrent edits. (9) AC-12 covers session resumption. (10) AC-15 covers the publish-transition lifecycle. CAVEAT: Without file contents I could not verify existing useContent signatures, return types, or how contentstack.ts currently initializes the SDK — these ACs may need refinement once the current API surface is known, particularly around how preview data is expected to merge with or replace published data.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Pipeline asymmetry: OpenSpec provided a valuable architectural insight (useContent as central hub for 236+ components) but did not fulfill its elaboration mandate — acceptChanged is false and no ACs were produced. Speckit compensated by building all 15 ACs from scratch, effectively performing both elaboration and hardening roles. The resulting ACs are well-structured (production safety layers, error/resilience scenarios, race conditions, regression gate for 236+ consumers, cross-codebase parity for GO/UP/MX), but Speckit explicitly caveats that it could not verify existing useContent signatures, return types, or Contentstack SDK initialization — meaning ACs may not align with the real API surface. Human review needed to (1) confirm ACs match actual useContent/useContentstack API contracts, (2) validate that OpenSpec's underperformance does not indicate a systemic issue with the agent pipeline for empty-AC stories.
